body:
## RomM Client 1.0.1

A fullscreen, controller-driven client for your [RomM](https://romm.app) server, for Windows and Linux. It syncs your platforms and games, downloads and caches the ROMs you play, installs and sets up the emulators for you, and keeps your saves in step with the server.

This is the first stable release, and the list below is everything RomM Client does today.

---

### Installing and updating the app
- **Windows:** an installer with two types: *Normal* (your user, Start menu entry, data in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\RomM-Client`) or *Portable* (any folder you pick, data in a `data` folder beside the program; delete the folder to remove it). Silent installs are supported (`/VERYSILENT`, `/PORTABLE=1`).
- **Linux (x64, Steam Deck / SteamOS):** a single AppImage that needs no install and no root. Data is kept in `~/.local/share/RomM-Client`.
- **Self-updating:** the app checks for a newer version at start-up and from **About → Check for updates**. You can download and install it (checked against the release's SHA-256 sums), be reminded later, or ignore that version. Your data is never touched. The check happens before **Who's playing?**, even with a single account, and is not repeated when you switch accounts.

### Your RomM server and library
- **Sign in** with a username and password, or a RomM client API token. Credentials are stored encrypted (Windows DPAPI, or an owner-only key file on Linux).
- **Accounts:** several users, or several servers, on one computer. Start-up shows **Who's playing?**; each account has its own settings, library, play history, stats and saves, while emulators and downloaded games, firmware, soundtracks and covers are shared. Removing an account asks for its own password.
- **Library sync:** platforms, games, covers and metadata are synced and saved to disk, so browsing works offline.
  - **Background sync:** a turning sign beside your name shows it is syncing; nothing covers the screen, and a click on it stops it.
  - **Who's playing:** the person you pick has their library synced under their picture (the rest of the screen fades) before the home page opens. Press Back to stop waiting.
  - **Collections** are synced with the rest, and when part of a sync fails the app says why instead of showing an empty list.
- **Browsing:** platforms grouped by manufacturer with a colour of their own, a **Continue playing** row, game rows with cover, regions, size and download state, other versions of a game ("Play version…"), and games that RomM files as saves are hidden.
- **Search:** an on-screen keyboard with live matches on a controller; type-ahead on a keyboard.
- **Soundtracks:** a game's soundtrack from the server streams while it downloads, plays while you browse, and can be saved for offline. Autoplay can be switched off.
- **Download ahead:** fetch an emulator, a core or a game before you want to play it.

### Playing games
- Pick a game and press **A**: the emulator (if missing) and the game are downloaded, firmware the server holds is fetched, and the game starts. Cached games start with no network.
- **Now playing screen:** cover, emulator, session clock, total and last play time, and live stages through to sending your saves. Close the game in the emulator, press **Stop game**, or hold **Back + Start** (Share + Options on a PlayStation pad).
- **Saves sync with your server**, per game and per emulator: memory cards, battery saves, save folders and, where the emulator allows it, **resume points**. Versions are kept, and one account's progress is never uploaded to another's server.
- **Resume points** (stop mid-game, carry on later) are on for RetroArch, DuckStation and PCSX2, per platform or per game.
- **When a game will not start, the message says why.** The app reads the log the emulator wrote and puts the cause in words: the exact ROM files an arcade set is missing (and that the set is probably from a different MAME version), or that a BIOS or firmware file is missing and has to be added on the platform in RomM. Other emulators' own error lines are shown too.
- **Firmware is checked before the game downloads** for the RetroArch systems that cannot start without it (3DO, PC-FX, Sega CD, CD-i, Intellivision, ColecoVision), as it already was for Xbox and PS3, with a message naming the file to add. A system whose core has a replacement or does not need it (Dreamcast, Saturn, Amiga, Atari 5200, Atari Lynx) is never blocked.
- **Firmware goes where each emulator reads it:** most RetroArch cores read the system folder, but Flycast (Dreamcast), Fuse (ZX Spectrum), FinalBurn Neo (Neo Geo), Kronos (Saturn) and SAME_CDi (CD-i) read a folder of their own, and the files are now put there.
- **Multi-file games:** RomM adds a playlist (.m3u) to the zip of a game kept as several files. When it only lists one disc (or one disc's own .cue and .bin or .iso files) the disc's .cue is launched, because some cores (Beetle PCE, Opera) cannot open a playlist; a playlist of several discs is still launched as a playlist.
- **Amstrad CPC Plus / GX4000 cartridges** (a .bin dump) play: the app wraps the dump as a .cpr, uses the CPC 6128+ model in 24-bit colour, and copes with an apostrophe in the file name (Caprice32 cannot open one).
- **Window size:** in windowed mode the size you drag the window to is remembered, and a window opens in the middle of the screen.
- **Game progress** (status, completion, rating) is set from the game's options and synced to the server.
- **Discord status** (off by default) shows the game, the platform and the emulator, without repeating the platform.
- **PSP and Xbox 360 extra content:** DLC held on the server in a game's `dlc` folder is installed into PPSSPP and Xenia Canary. Xbox 360 packages are checked first (header, size and every block against the package's hashes), must be for the game being started, and a bad one is reported once and left out. **PS3 game updates** can be looked up, downloaded from Sony (or from your server's `update` folder), checked and installed into RPCS3.

### Supported emulators
Installed and configured automatically, each inside its own folder. Every one has been played with a real pad on Windows (an 8BitDo, and a DualShock 4 for all but melonDS; see `docs/CONTROLLERS.md`).

| Platforms | Emulator | Saves sync | Resume points |
|---|---|---|---|
| NES, SNES, N64, Game Boy / Color / Advance, Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear, Mega CD, 32X, Saturn, Dreamcast, Atari (2600, 5200, 7800, Lynx, Jaguar), PC Engine, PC-FX, Neo Geo, arcade, 3DO, CD-i, WonderSwan, ColecoVision, Intellivision, Commodore 64 / 128 / Plus/4 / PET / VIC-20, Amstrad CPC, Amiga, ZX Spectrum, DOS, Doom and more | RetroArch + libretro cores | Yes | Yes |
| PlayStation | DuckStation | Yes | Yes |
| PlayStation 2 | PCSX2 | Yes | Yes |
| PlayStation 3 | RPCS3 | Yes (by title ID) | No |
| PSP | PPSSPP | Yes | No |
| GameCube, Wii | Dolphin (Wii Remote + Nunchuk on your pad; pointer by right stick or motion) | Yes | No |
| Wii U | Cemu | Yes | No (Cemu has no save states) |
| DS | melonDS | Yes | No |
| 3DS | Azahar | Yes | No (Azahar advises against save states) |
| Xbox | xemu | Yes | No |
| Xbox 360 | Xenia Canary | Yes | No |

Nintendo Switch is intentionally not included.

### Emulator setup, options and updates
- **Choose the emulator** for a whole platform or a single game, from the ones that can really play it (for example Mega Drive on Genesis Plus GX, PicoDrive or BlastEm). A warning appears before you switch away from a game that has progress.
- **Options:** common settings for every emulator as simple lists (resolution, aspect ratio, graphics API, vsync and so on), per platform or per game, with the default shown. The app writes them into the emulator's settings and puts the emulator's default back when you stop choosing one. Plus **extra arguments** for anything else.
  - Cemu: graphics API, vsync, upscaling filter, volume, downscale filter, frame-rate overlay and Wii U language. xemu: **graphics renderer (OpenGL or Vulkan)**. melonDS: DS name, language, colour and birthday.
- **Top-bar pages and a platform manager:** the menu is four pages on the top bar. **Library** (sync, accounts, server), **Emulators** (updates, controller test, install or remove any emulator or RetroArch core), **Settings** (fullscreen, autoplay and, per account, Discord status and Button style) and **About** (updates, feedback, Quit). Press Options on a platform for its manager page: its settings, and every emulator that can play it to use, install, update or remove.
- **Emulator updates:** the app looks for newer emulators and RetroArch cores at start-up, at most once a week (a "Checking emulators" sign shows), from **Emulators → Check for emulator updates**, and from a platform's manager page. Tick what to update and they download side by side; settings and saves are kept.
- **The same cores as RomM's web player:** for each system RomM plays in the browser, the first core RetroArch uses here is the one the browser uses (so progress is the same kind of save), the other cores RomM offers are choices, and every name RomM files a system under is recognised. PlayStation, PSP and DS keep their own emulators and also offer RomM's cores.
- **Versions:** the Emulators page and a platform's manager page show the version installed (``v1.22.2``, ``2609b``) beside its date, RetroArch cores included, and an update says which version it replaces.
- **Saves filed the way RomM's player files them:** RetroArch's saves and states are listed on the server under the core's plain name (`stella2014`) instead of `retroarch-stella2014`, so RomM's browser player and this app share them. Older ones are still found and re-filed under the new name when they are next uploaded. A RetroArch state is named the way RomM's player names its states (`Space Invaders [2026-11-21 14-52-58-014].state`), the newest state of a game is its resume point whichever of the two saved it, and a state saved in the browser is never written over.
- **The sign-in renews itself:** RomM's access token runs out after a while, so when one has expired the app signs in again by itself and carries on (an API key has no password to do that with).
- **Stable builds:** RetroArch and its cores come from libretro's stable release, so you are not offered a new nightly every day. libretro publishes the cores as one large archive (about 230 MB) that has to be decoded from the front for any core, so the first core you install downloads it and takes about half a minute to unpack, saving every core the app offers as a small zip (about 140 MB); after that any core installs in a moment.
- The emulators' own "an update is available" boxes are switched off, so only the app asks.
- **Cemu (Wii U)** gets its keys from your server, a controller profile for the pad you hold, sound on the default device, rumble, and Discord presence off so it does not clash with the app's own.

### Controllers
- **Hints follow your pad:** the footer shows Xbox, PlayStation or Nintendo button names for whatever you used last.
- **Controls: Emulator's own or Custom**, per platform (platform manager → **Controls**). Emulator's own is the default: the emulator reads your controller itself and you set it up in its own input settings; the first game on a platform shows a note saying so. Custom has RomM Client map your controller and lets you remap it on the controller screen.
- **One switch for RetroArch:** Emulators -> RetroArch -> **Controls for every RetroArch platform** flips every platform RetroArch plays between the emulator's own controls and Custom, without touching what you remapped.
- **Controller screen** for every platform (Controls → Custom): the console's own controller (drawn for every console, including the Amiga CD32, Intellivision, Vectrex, Pokémon Mini and CD-i; only the Commodore PET, DOS and Doom use a standard gamepad) on one side, your pad's button for each control on the other. Change any control by pressing the button you want, or step through choices; each pad keeps its own choices per platform. Used by RetroArch, DuckStation, PCSX2, RPCS3, Dolphin, Azahar, melonDS, xemu, PPSSPP, Xenia and Cemu.
- **Button style** (Settings): choose Xbox, PlayStation or Nintendo and every hint and picture uses it whatever you press; leave it on Automatic and they follow the controller you used last.
- **Controller test** (Emulators page): press every button and move every stick and see each one register, with the pad's identity and raw inputs. Can be sent as a problem report.
- **Unknown pads:** a pad the system does not recognise is named and laid out from a built-in controller database, and given to the emulators too.
- With **Custom**, emulators are set up for the pad in use, not a default: pad profiles for Cemu, RetroArch, RPCS3, xemu, PPSSPP, melonDS, Xenia and the rest.

### Feedback and reports
- **Report a problem** is a short step-by-step form: pick the area, a title, how to make it happen, an optional email, then **review exactly what will be sent**. For an emulator problem you pick the exact emulator or RetroArch core. Every report gets a short reference (like `K7QM-2XDF`).
- **Send feedback**, and a **Send error report** button on failure dialogs. Nothing is sent unless you choose it; server addresses, user names, computer and folder names are removed first, and your library and saves are never included.
- Reports go to the project's own service by default; set `ReportsUrl` to `"off"` to remove the options.

### A note about Linux
The Linux version is built and runs, but it has had far less testing than Windows. The controller setup in particular has only been tried on Windows, with Xbox-style and PlayStation pads. Games have been played with a pad in RetroArch, RPCS3, xemu, PPSSPP, melonDS, Dolphin, DuckStation, PCSX2, Xenia, Azahar and Cemu. If you try any of it on Linux, please tell us how it goes from About → Send feedback.

### Known issues
- **Systems added from RomM's list of browser-playable systems** use the same cores RomM does. Played by hand: 3DO, Amiga, Amiga CD32, Amstrad CPC, ZX Spectrum, Atari 5200, CD-i and Neo Geo (the Commodore 128, PET and VIC-20 share their emulator with the 64, which was). **Not yet tried by hand:** DOS, Doom, Neo Geo Pocket, Pokémon Mini, PC-FX, ColecoVision, Intellivision, Vectrex and WonderSwan. Flash (Ruffle) is not supported.
- **Arcade needs a MAME 0.78 / 2003-Plus set.** The core is MAME 2003-Plus, so a ROM set from a newer MAME (the usual download) may be missing files or have different versions of them and will not start; the message then lists the files it could not find. Use a Full Non-Merged set made for MAME 2003-Plus, kept zipped. Games that need CHD files are not supported yet. Neo Geo needs `neogeo.zip` as firmware on its platform.
- **Emulator's own controls:** a freshly installed PCSX2, DuckStation or Cemu has no controller bound until you bind one in the emulator's own input settings (or choose **Custom** for that platform). The first game on each platform says so.
- **Steam running with a PlayStation pad (Windows):** Steam Input can make sticks and triggers laggy or stuck in emulators. Turn off *Enable Steam Input for PlayStation Controllers* in Steam's controller settings, or quit Steam before playing. See the README for details.
- **Azahar (3DS)** will not open its window while a Bluetooth Nintendo pad (an N64 pad was seen) is connected: switch that pad off before starting a 3DS game.
- Azahar's sticks can be swapped but not changed one direction at a time; xemu cannot move a stick or trigger to another axis; melonDS cannot bind triggers or sticks as DS buttons.
- PPSSPP controls are not set up on Linux, nor for a pad that is neither Xbox-style nor PlayStation.
